title: Service-account token audiences are enforced — every `boundServiceAccountToken` authentication must map an audience (CVE-2026-77524)
quote: KEDA 2.21 defaults to `operator.serviceAccountTokens.mode: enforce-audience`. This is a breaking change for Vault Kubernetes authentication and **all** `boundServiceAccountToken` (BSAT) authentication, not just Vault. Missing approvals or service-account audience mappings fail the affected authentication. The operator can remain healthy while individual scalers fail.
remediation: Each TriggerAuthentication / ClusterTriggerAuthentication named mints a bound service-account token. After the hop the operator (chart default `operator.serviceAccountTokens.mode: enforce-audience`) refuses to mint one without an exact namespace/name → audience mapping in `permissions.operator.restrict.serviceAccountTokenCreationRoles`, and the receiving scaler (metrics-api, Prometheus, Loki, Datadog Cluster Agent, …) fails to authenticate while the operator stays healthy. Before upgrading: map each service account to a non-API audience the receiver accepts (kube-rbac-proxy `--auth-token-audiences`), and verify readiness on every ScaledObject that references the authentication. `mode: legacy` is an operator-wide, insecure escape hatch, not a per-object fix. Datadog Cluster Agent 7.83.2 cannot accept a custom audience — use API/app-key auth there.
verifyCommand: kubectl get triggerauthentications.keda.sh,clustertriggerauthentications.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.boundServiceAccountToken != null) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name) serviceAccounts=\([.spec.boundServiceAccountToken[].serviceAccountName] | unique | join(","))"'  # each row needs an audience mapping for every service account listed before the hop

title: Service-account token audiences are enforced — Vault Kubernetes authentication must log in with a dedicated projected token (CVE-2026-77524)
quote: KEDA 2.21 defaults to `operator.serviceAccountTokens.mode: enforce-audience`. This is a breaking change for Vault Kubernetes authentication and **all** `boundServiceAccountToken` (BSAT) authentication, not just Vault. Missing approvals or service-account audience mappings fail the affected authentication. The operator can remain healthy while individual scalers fail.
remediation: Each TriggerAuthentication / ClusterTriggerAuthentication named logs in to Vault with a Kubernetes service-account token. After the hop the operator no longer forwards its own API token: the 2.21 chart projects a dedicated token (`hashiCorpVault.kubernetesAuth.audience: vault`, mounted at `/var/run/secrets/keda-vault`), and the Vault role must accept that audience. Per object: omit the whole `credential` block (or set `credential.serviceAccount: /var/run/secrets/keda-vault/token`); a `credential.serviceAccountName` needs an audience mapping for that service account; an existing extra-volume token needs its audience approved via `operator.serviceAccountTokens.additionalAllowedAudiences`. Leaving the old API-token path, or `credential: {}`, fails the login.
verifyCommand: kubectl get triggerauthentications.keda.sh,clustertriggerauthentications.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.hashiCorpVault.authentication == "kubernetes") | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name) credential=\(.spec.hashiCorpVault.credential // {} | keys | join(","))"'  # each row logs in to Vault with a service-account token; credential=serviceAccount/serviceAccountName shows which path it selects

title: keda-operator: chart 2.21 defaults to `operator.serviceAccountTokens.mode: enforce-audience` — Helm values must carry the audience mappings

detection.reason: the operator's Helm values (operator.serviceAccountTokens.*, hashiCorpVault.kubernetesAuth.*, permissions.operator.restrict.serviceAccountTokenCreationRoles) are rendered into args, env and projected volumes the projection does not carry

quote: Inventory both TriggerAuthentications and ClusterTriggerAuthentications using `spec.hashiCorpVault.authentication: kubernetes` or `spec.boundServiceAccountToken`. Review default and explicit token paths, existing extra volumes, and token-creation RBAC.
remediation: Platform side of CVE-2026-77524. Before the chart upgrade: inventory the TA/CTAs that use `hashiCorpVault.authentication: kubernetes` or `boundServiceAccountToken` (the two app-side rules name them); choose audiences the API server does NOT accept and configure each receiver for them; give Vault its own TokenReview credential; write `permissions.operator.restrict.serviceAccountTokenCreationRoles[]` with `name`, `namespace` AND `audience` per service account (an entry without `audience` grants RBAC only; `allowAllServiceAccountTokenCreation: true` still needs exact mappings); upgrade chart and operator together, never with `--reuse-values` alone (older saved values omit the new defaults — pass `hashiCorpVault.kubernetesAuth.audience` and `projectedTokenMountPath` explicitly, or use `--reset-then-reuse-values`). Afterwards verify ScaledObject readiness and failure Events, not just `helm --wait`. `mode: legacy` + `additionalAllowedAudiences: []` + `hashiCorpVault.kubernetesAuth.audience: ""` restores the old behaviour cluster-wide and leaves the privilege escalation open — temporary only; legacy mode with any configured audience entry is rejected.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[].image | test("kedacore/keda(:|@|$)")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) env=\([.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN|VAULT")) | .name] | join(",")) volumes=\([.spec.template.spec.volumes[]? | select(.projected != null) | .name] | join(","))"'  # the operator Deployment; after the chart upgrade expect KEDA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_* env and a keda-vault projected volume (names only, never values)
coversNotes: Vault using the operator service account

title: Temporal: `buildId`, `selectAllActive` and `selectUnversioned` are removed — the scaler refuses the trigger

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: KEDA 2.21 removes the deprecated Temporal scaler settings `buildId`, `selectAllActive`, and `selectUnversioned`. A ScaledObject or ScaledJob containing any of these fields now fails scaler metadata parsing.
remediation: Each temporal trigger named still sets one of the three. From 2.21 the tags are `deprecated=` and scaler metadata parsing fails, so the ScaledObject / ScaledJob stops scaling after the hop. For unversioned workers delete the settings; for versioned workers configure `workerDeploymentName` and `workerDeploymentBuildId` (one scaling resource per deployment version that needs its own behaviour).
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select(.type == "temporal" and ((.metadata // {}) | has("buildId") or has("selectAllActive") or has("selectUnversioned"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type) keys=\(.metadata | keys | map(select(. == "buildId" or . == "selectAllActive" or . == "selectUnversioned")) | join(","))"'  # each row fails scaler metadata parsing on the hop

title: Azure Pipelines: new `scaleOnInFlight` defaults to true — the queue length now counts assigned, unfinished jobs

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: KEDA 2.21 adds the Azure Pipelines scaler metadata field `scaleOnInFlight`, which defaults to `true`. The reported queue length now includes unfinished jobs that have already been assigned to an agent. Finished jobs remain excluded.
remediation: Each azure-pipelines trigger named changes its metric on the hop unless `scaleOnInFlight` is set explicitly. Keep the default (`true`) on a ScaledJob using the `default` scaling strategy — it avoids subtracting running jobs twice; set `scaleOnInFlight: false` (with the `accurate` ScaledJob strategy) to count only unassigned jobs as 2.20 did; for a ScaledObject decide whether assigned work belongs in the replica count and test it. A trigger that already sets the key is listed too and needs no edit.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select(.type == "azure-pipelines") | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type) scaleOnInFlight=\(.metadata.scaleOnInFlight // null)"'  # each row's metric changes on the hop unless scaleOnInFlight is set; scaleOnInFlight=null means the new default applies

title: Liiklus trigger is deprecated — removal planned for 2.24 (upstream project unmaintained)

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: The Liiklus scaler is deprecated because the upstream project is unmaintained. Its code is planned for removal in a later KEDA release. See #7929.
remediation: From v2.21.0 the liiklus scaler carries a deprecatedAnnounce tag ("will be removed in v2.24") and the operator emits a KEDAScalerInfo event on each ScaledObject / ScaledJob named. They keep working on this hop; plan the move to the `kafka` trigger (Liiklus fronts Kafka) before 2.24.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select(.type == "liiklus") | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row uses a trigger type planned for removal in 2.24
